subject: Re: Crestline PO & billing rhythm — PO per invoice, net terms, and slab discount
thread_summary: Crestline procurement asked about PO requirements (PO per invoice), preferred net45, and requested slab discounts for committed spend. Internal negotiation on offering tiered discounts vs concession on net terms; agreed to provide SOW, W-9 and a counterproposal for consolidated monthly invoice referencing PO numbers.
messages:
From: Megan Tran <megan.tran@crestlinehealth.com>
To: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.inference> , ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.inference>
Cc: procurement@crestlinehealth.com
Date: Tue, 24 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: PO requirements + invoice cadence questions for Redwood pilot

Hi Kimberly / Ben,

Thanks again for the product demo last week — the team is excited to start the pilot. Procurement needs a few clarifications before we can raise a PO:

- Do you require a separate PO for each invoice, or can we reference one blanket PO for the month? Our AP system prefers one PO per invoice but we can be flexible with justification.
- What net terms do you support? Our standard is net45, but we can sometimes do net30 for strategic vendors.
- Do you offer committed-volume discounts (slab pricing) if we commit to an annual spend target?

Can you also share your W-9 and the SOW so procurement can match to the PO?

Appreciate a quick reply — procurement wants the payment terms and invoice rhythm captured before we approve the pilot budget.

Best,
Megan
Megan Tran
Senior Program Manager — Vendor Ops
Crestline Health

From: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.inference>

Subject: Re: PO requirements + invoice cadence questions for Redwood pilot

Hi Megan — thanks for the clear list. Quick answers up front and attaching our W-9: Redwood_W9.pdf (see attachment).

- PO per invoice: We can do either, but our preference is a single invoice per month with a PO reference field that lists the PO number(s). If your AP requires a strict one-PO-per-invoice system, we can accommodate by including the PO number on each invoice line item.
- Net terms: Standard is net30; we can extend to net45 for enterprise deals with a committed spending agreement.
- Slab discounts: Yes — we typically handle tiered discounts based on committed annual spend. I'll follow up with a proposed tiering.

I attached a first-pass SOW (SOW_Crestline_v1.pdf) to make it easier for procurement to map scope to invoice items. If procurement has a vendor form, please send and we'll complete it.

Thanks — would it help if Ben and Marissa jump on a 20-minute call with procurement to iron out PO/invoice mapping?

—Kimberly Park
Head of Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Attachment: Redwood_W9.pdf, SOW_Crestline_v1.pdf

Kimberly / team —

Quick procurement note on Crestline policy so we're all aligned:
- We require a PO number on every invoice. Blanket POs are allowed but our AP still expects the PO listed on the invoice document itself.
- Preferred payment term is net45; net30 requires additional business justification.
- Invoices must be issued by the 5th business day of the month covering the previous month's usage (so Dec invoices should arrive by Jan 5).
- For any discounts tied to committed spend, procurement needs the slab definitions in the master quote and the contract.

I've attached our procurement form (Crestline_procurement_form.pdf) that needs to be completed for vendor onboarding. Also, please include remittance details and W-9 when you return the completed form.

Thanks — Carlos
Carlos Ruiz
Procurement Manager
Crestline Health

Attachment: Crestline_procurement_form.pdf

From: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.inference>
To: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.inference>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.inference>, rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.inference>
Date: Mon, 29 Nov 2026 09:03:00 -0800
Subject: INTERNAL: Crestline ask — discount slabs vs net45 concession

Team — quick internal on strategy for CRESTLINE (DEAL-7831):

Context: procurement wants PO on every invoice and prefers net45. They asked for slab discounts by committed annual spend. We need to decide whether to concede net45 or require net30 in exchange for deeper discounts. Rishi, how much margin headroom do we have if we move to net45?

Proposed public position:
- Offer tiered discounts: 8% at $150k yearly, 12% at $300k, 18% at $600k.
- Allow net45 only if they commit to a 12-month minimum and a 15% uplift in monthly committed spend for the first 3 months (to reduce short-term cash impact).
- Accept PO-on-each-invoice (we can include a PO reference field and pass-through remittance).

If finance can't swallow net45 at those discounts, alternative: keep net30 and offer a one-time onboarding credit instead of higher slab percentages.

Thoughts? I think meeting halfway keeps the deal moving while protecting cash.

—Ben

From: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.inference>
To: Carlos Ruiz <c.ruiz@crestlinehealth.com>, Megan Tran <megan.tran@crestlinehealth.com>
Cc: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.inference>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.inference>, rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.inference>
Date: Tue, 30 Nov 2026 10:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: PO requirements + invoice cadence questions for Redwood pilot

Hi Carlos / Megan — thanks for the procurement form, Carlos. We completed the Crestline form and attached it here along with the SOW and our W-9. See attachments: Crestline_procurement_form.pdf (completed), SOW_Crestline_v1.pdf, Redwood_W9.pdf.

Counterproposal (to align with your net45 preference while protecting both parties):
- Invoice cadence: Redwood will issue a single consolidated monthly invoice by the 5th business day of the following month. Each invoice will include a dedicated PO reference field and will list the specific PO number(s) you supply. We can also include a line-level PO reference if your AP requires that.
- Net terms: We will accept net45 for this engagement provided Crestline commits to a 12-month term and an annual committed spend of at least $300,000.
- Discounts: We propose slab pricing as follows (applies to consumed usage billed during the committed period):
   * 10% discount at $200,000 annualized spend
   * 15% discount at $400,000 annualized spend
   * 20% discount at $750,000 annualized spend
- Onboarding concession: If Crestline prefers net30 instead, we can offer a one-time 5% onboarding credit applied to the first invoice instead of the expanded slab.

Attached: Quote_DEAL-7831.pdf with the slab math and examples, SOW_Crestline_v1.pdf, Redwood_W9.pdf.

If that looks reasonable, we can send a DocuSign with the master quote + PO terms and get procurement to confirm the PO numbering convention. Ben/Marissa — please flag if finance needs different language on remittance/late fees. Rishi, can you confirm the net45 with the proposed slab at $300k is acceptable from a cash-flow perspective?

Best,
Kimberly Park
Head of Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Attachments: Quote_DEAL-7831.pdf, SOW_Crestline_v1.pdf, Redwood_W9.pdf
